gloss: one sun (approx. 3.03 cm); a tiny amount; a very short distance

definitions.gloss: one sun (approx. 3.03 cm); a tiny amount; a very short distance

examples.japanese: {一寸|いっすん}{法師|ぼうし}のお{話|はなし}を{知|し}っていますか。
examples.english: Do you know the story of Issun-bōshi (the one-inch boy)?

examples.japanese: {一寸|いっすん}の{虫|むし}にも{五分|ごぶ}の{魂|たましい}。
examples.english: Even a tiny insect has a soul. (Even the weakest have their pride.)

examples.japanese: {一寸|いっすん}{先|さき}は{闇|やみ}というように、{未来|みらい}のことは{誰|だれ}にも{分|わ}からない。
examples.english: As the saying goes, 'darkness lies an inch ahead' — nobody can know the future.

notes:
A traditional Japanese unit of length equal to approximately 3.03 centimeters (about 1.2 inches). Part of the {尺貫法|しゃっかんほう} system of traditional measurement. Today mainly encountered in set phrases, proverbs, and cultural references.

FAMOUS PHRASES:
- {一寸|いっすん}{法師|ぼうし}: Issun-bōshi, the fairy tale of a boy only one sun tall (similar to Tom Thumb)
- {一寸|いっすん}の{虫|むし}にも{五分|ごぶ}の{魂|たましい}: even a worm will turn (literally: even a one-sun insect has half a soul)
- {一寸|いっすん}{先|さき}は{闇|やみ}: the future is unpredictable (literally: darkness lies one sun ahead)

PRONUNCIATION:
The kanji {一寸|いっすん} can also be read as ちょっと in casual writing, meaning "a little bit." Context determines the reading: in measurement or set phrases, it is いっすん; when used as an adverb meaning "a bit," it is ちょっと.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寸|すん}: sun (the unit itself)
- {尺|しゃく}: shaku — a larger traditional unit (about 30.3 cm, or 10 sun)
- ちょっと: a little — the colloquial reading of the same kanji
